## 23.1 PyCall.jl: Calling PySAL from Julia

While SpatialStats.jl and SpatialReg.jl are under development, PyCall.jl provides a production-grade bridge to Python's PySAL suite. The following patterns demonstrate how to seamlessly call PySAL's spreg module from Julia workflows, with automatic data conversion between Julia DataFrames and Python/NumPy objects.

```julia
# === PyCall bridge for PySAL spatial regression ===
# Install PyCall and configure Python environment:
# ] add PyCall
# ENV["PYTHON"] = "/usr/bin/python3"  # or conda env python
# ] build PyCall
using PyCall, SparseArrays, DataFrames
# Import PySAL modules (lazy — only loaded once per session)
const libpysal = PyNULL()
const spreg    = PyNULL()
const esda     = PyNULL()
const numpy    = PyNULL()
function __init__()
copy!(libpysal, pyimport("libpysal"))
copy!(spreg,    pyimport("spreg"))
copy!(esda,     pyimport("esda"))
copy!(numpy,    pyimport("numpy"))
end
"""
```

Convert Julia SparseMatrixCSC to PySAL W (weights) object.

PySAL W takes a Dict{Int, Vector{Int}} of neighbor lists.

"""

```julia
function to_pysal_w(W::SparseMatrixCSC{Float64})
n = size(W, 1)
# Build Python dict: {i: [j, ...]} for each row i
neighbors_dict = Dict{Int,Vector{Int}}()
weights_dict   = Dict{Int,Vector{Float64}}()
for i in 1:n
js, ws = findnz(W[i, :])
neighbors_dict[i-1] = js .- 1   # Python 0-indexed
weights_dict[i-1]   = ws
end
py_w = libpysal.weights.W(neighbors_dict, weights_dict)
py_w.transform = "R"  # Ensure row-standardized
return py_w
end
"""
```

Estimate Spatial Lag Model via PySAL GM_Lag from Julia.

Returns NamedTuple compatible with Julia workflow.

"""

```julia
function pysal_slm(
y::Vector{Float64},
```

X::Matrix{Float64},

W::SparseMatrixCSC{Float64};

var_names::Vector{String} = ["x$(i)" for i in 1:size(X,2)]

)

py_w   = to_pysal_w(W)

py_y   = numpy.array(reshape(y, :, 1))

py_X   = numpy.array(X)

model = spreg.GM_Lag(

py_y, py_X;

w         = py_w,

name_y    = "outcome",

name_x    = var_names,

robust    = "white"    # HC robust standard errors

)

```julia
# Convert Python results back to Julia types
return (
rho    = Float64(model.rho),
betas  = Float64.(vec(model.betas)),
std_err= Float64.(vec(model.std_err)),
t_stat = Float64.(vec(model.z_stat[:, 1])),
p_val  = Float64.(vec(model.z_stat[:, 2])),
pr2    = Float64(model.pr2),
```

AIC    = Float64(model.aic),

fitted = Float64.(vec(model.predy)),

resids = Float64.(vec(model.u)),

)

```julia
end
"""
```

Compute LISA via PySAL esda.Moran_Local from Julia.

"""

```julia
function pysal_lisa(
values::Vector{Float64},
```

W::SparseMatrixCSC{Float64};

permutations::Int = 999,

alpha::Float64 = 0.05,

seed::Int = 42

)

py_w = to_pysal_w(W)

py_v = numpy.array(values)

ml = esda.Moran_Local(py_v, py_w;

permutations = permutations,

seed         = seed

)

```julia
# ml.q: LISA quadrant (1=HH, 2=LH, 3=LL, 4=HL)
quad_map = Dict(1=>:HH, 2=>:LH, 3=>:LL, 4=>:HL)
p_sims   = Float64.(ml.p_sim)
quads    = Int.(ml.q)
clusters = [p_sims[i] < alpha ? get(quad_map, quads[i], :NS) : :NS
for i in 1:length(values)]
return (
```

I_local  = Float64.(ml.Is),

p_values = p_sims,

cluster  = clusters,

z_scores = Float64.(ml.z_sim),

)


## 23.2 RCall.jl: Calling spdep and CARBayes from Julia

```julia
end
# === RCall bridge for spdep and CARBayes ===
using RCall, DataFrames
"""
```

Run complete spatial regression workflow via R's spdep/spatialreg.

Includes: OLS + LM tests, SLM, SEM, compare AIC.

"""

```julia
function r_spatial_workflow(
y::Vector{Float64},
```

X::DataFrame,

W::Matrix{Float64};

var_names::Vector{String} = names(X)

)

```julia
# Pass data to R
@rput y W
for (col, nm) in zip(eachcol(X), var_names)
```

R"assign($(nm), $(col))"

```julia
end
formula_str = "y ~ " * join(var_names, " + ")
@rput formula_str
R"""
library(spdep)
library(spatialreg)
# Convert dense W to spdep listw object
```

W_list <- mat2listw(W, style='W')

```julia
# OLS model
formula <- as.formula(formula_str)
ols_mod <- lm(formula)
# LM tests for spatial specification
lm_tests <- lm.LMtests(ols_mod, listw=W_list,
test=c('LMlag','LMerr','RLMlag','RLMerr'))
# Fit both spatial models
slm_mod <- lagsarlm(formula, listw=W_list, Durbin=FALSE)
sem_mod <- errorsarlm(formula, listw=W_list)
# Summary stats
results <- list(
ols_aic  = AIC(ols_mod),
slm_rho  = slm_mod$rho,
slm_aic  = AIC(slm_mod),
sem_lam  = sem_mod$lambda,
sem_aic  = AIC(sem_mod),
lm_lag   = lm_tests$LMlag$statistic,
p_lag    = lm_tests$LMlag$p.value,
lm_err   = lm_tests$LMerr$statistic,
p_err    = lm_tests$LMerr$p.value,
preferred= if(AIC(slm_mod) < AIC(sem_mod)) 'SLM' else 'SEM'
)
"""
@rget results
return results
end
"""
```

Fit Bayesian BYM disease mapping model via R's CARBayes.

Much simpler interface than Turing.jl for standard disease mapping.

"""

```julia
function r_bym_model(
observed::Vector{Int},
expected::Vector{Float64},
```

W_bin::Matrix{Bool};

n_iter::Int = 20_000,

burnin::Int  = 5_000

)

```julia
@rput observed expected W_bin n_iter burnin
R"""
library(CARBayes)
formula <- observed ~ offset(log(expected))
model <- S.CARbym(
formula  = formula,
family   = 'poisson',
```

W        = W_bin * 1L,   # CARBayes wants integer matrix

burnin   = burnin,

n.sample = n_iter,

verbose  = FALSE

)

rr_mean  <- model$fitted.values / expected

rr_lower <- model$summary.results[, 'Lower'&& '2.5%']  # approx

"""

```julia
@rget rr_mean
return rr_mean
end
```
